issues.legal_issue: An arbitration award is without jurisdiction when the arbitrator was appointed under the contractual arbitration procedure pursuant to a court order, but the asserted arbitration agreement was not executed by the government and the government was not a party to the suit that produced the order.
material_facts: The property owner signed an agreement providing for arbitration, but neither the central nor the provincial government executed it.
A court ordered the agreement to be filed and required arbitration; the Union of India was not a party to that suit.
The orders appointing the arbitrators who conducted and completed the arbitration referred to the agreement and the earlier suit, but did not appoint them under the statutory compensation power.
The final arbitrator made an award that the property owner challenged as without jurisdiction.
issues.conclusion: The final arbitrator was appointed under Section 20(4) of the Arbitration Act, 1940, in pursuance of the earlier court order, rather than under Section 19 of the Defence of India Act, 1939. Because the asserted agreement was not executed by either government and the Union of India was not a party to the earlier suit, the appointment and resulting award were without jurisdiction.
issues.legal_principle: Section 20(4) of the Arbitration Act, 1940 could not support the appointment in these circumstances: the appointment orders were made pursuant to the earlier court order and on the footing of an agreement that neither government had executed, while the Union of India was not a party to the suit in which that order was made. Section 19 of the Defence of India Act, 1939 provided a distinct statutory basis for appointment and compensation, but the later appointment orders did not invoke it; the fact that notices referred to Section 19 did not establish that the appointments were made under that provision. No earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: challenged_arbitration_award and appointment_pursuant_to_court_arbitration_order and government_unsigned_arbitration_agreement and government_not_party_to_underlying_suit and appointment_not_made_under_statutory_compensation_power

predicates.challenged_arbitration_award: A party to a proceeding challenging an arbitration award contends that the award is invalid for want of jurisdiction.
predicates.appointment_pursuant_to_court_arbitratio: The arbitrator was appointed pursuant to a court order directing arbitration under an asserted agreement.
predicates.government_unsigned_arbitration_agreemen: The government against which the arbitration is pursued did not execute the asserted arbitration agreement.
predicates.government_not_party_to_underlying_suit: The government against which the arbitration is pursued was not a party to the suit that produced the court order directing arbitration.
predicates.appointment_not_made_under_statutory_com: The appointment order did not appoint the arbitrator under the statutory power for determining compensation.

issues.definition: When an arbitration award is challenged and the arbitrator was appointed pursuant to a court order based on an agreement the government did not execute, the government was not a party to the underlying suit, and the appointment was not made under the statutory compensation power, the award is without jurisdiction.
